page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highcpu-80 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an Intel x86_64 processor. It features 80 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 40 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 160 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix operations. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance type.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core performance, with the instance placing in the top 25% for multi-core CPU stress tests and Passmark CPU evaluations. The architecture excels in parallelized workloads, demonstrating top-tier performance in static web serving throughput at 102.77 GB/sec and image processing. Memory bandwidth is also highly efficient, reaching 286.55 GB/sec for large-block read operations. For artificial intelligence workloads, the hardware-assisted AMX instructions support strong prompt processing speeds, achieving 261.35 tokens per second on medium-sized 7B parameter models.

The primary tradeoff of the n4-highcpu-80 is its low memory-to-core ratio of 2 GB per vCPU, which makes it less suitable for memory-intensive databases or large in-memory analytics. However, for compute-bound applications, it offers high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency by delivering strong multi-threaded performance without the added cost of excess memory. This instance is highly suited for software compilation, high-throughput web serving, image processing, multi-threaded decompression, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
